key_insight: Zero-shot LLMs improved the precision–yield trade-off for identifying interstitial lung disease (ILD) in oncology patients compared with published claims-based algorithms.
clinical_relevance: More accurate ILD identification could strengthen safety studies of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody–drug conjugates, rather than directly support cancer drug discovery.
method: Compared 12 open-access LLMs with 20 published claims-based algorithms.
Provided claims, clinical notes, or both without task-specific training.
Measured positive predictive value (PPV) and classification yield, then modeled drug-safety signal attenuation.
evidence_signal: Among 309 patients with ILD diagnosis codes adjudicated by two pulmonologists, claims-only Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% PPV at 4.9% yield for the highest-PPV algorithm.
watch_item: Validation beyond this single-health-system, diagnosis-code-selected cohort is needed; projected drug-safety and sample-size benefits were simulated, not observed.
paper_title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
